'''''Nymphaea candida''''' is a species of perennial, aquatic,<ref name = "Zhou et al., 2025" /> rhizomatous herb<ref name = "FinBIF" /> in the family [[Nymphaeaceae]] native to the region spanning from Europe to Siberia and Western Himalaya.<ref name = "POWO">''Nymphaea candida'' C.Presl. (n.d.). Plants of the World Online. Retrieved March 19, 2025, from https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:605520-1</ref>

===Vegetative characteristics===
''Nymphaea candida'' is a perennial, aquatic,<ref name = "Zhou et al., 2025" /> rhizomatous herb<ref name = "FinBIF">''Nymphaea candida''. (n.d.). Finnish Biodiversity Info Facility. Retrieved March 19, 2025, from https://laji.fi/en/taxon/MX.37841</ref> with unbranched,<ref name = "Flora of China">''Nymphaea candida'' in Flora of China @ efloras.org. (n.d.). Retrieved March 19, 2025, from http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=200007086</ref> 5 cm wide rhizomes.<ref name = "Conard, 1905" /> The petiolate, stipulate,<ref name = "FinBIF" /> oval to suborbicular floating leaf with an entire margin<ref name = "Conard, 1905" /> and a deep basal sinus<ref name = "Flora of Pakistan">''Nymphaea candida'' in Flora of Pakistan @ efloras.org. (n.d.). Retrieved March 19, 2025, from http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=5&taxon_id=200007086</ref> is 10–30 cm long, and 25 cm wide.<ref name = "Conard, 1905" /> The oblong submerged leaves have a thin lamina and short petioles.<ref name = "FinBIF" /> The thick, terete,<ref name = "FinBIF" /> smooth,<ref name = "Conard, 1905" /> 30–100(–160) cm long petiole<ref name = "Pflanzen in Deutschland">Glänzende Seerose - ''Nymphaea candida''. (n.d.). Pflanzen in Deutschland - Das Umfassende Pflanzenportal Für Die Heimische Flora. Retrieved March 19, 2025, from https://www.pflanzen-deutschland.de/Nymphaea_candida.html</ref> has air canals.<ref name = "FinBIF" />
===Generative characteristics===
The bisexual,<ref name = "Pflanzen in Deutschland" /> actinomorphic, 5–15 cm wide flower<ref name = "FinBIF" /> floats on the water surface.<ref name = "Flora of China" /> The 4(–5) oblong to ovate-oblong sepals are 3.8 cm long, and 1.3 cm wide. The 12–20 white petals<ref name = "Conard, 1905">Conard,  Henry S. (1905). The waterlilies: a monograph of the genus ''Nymphaea'' (pp. 172–173). Pub. by the Carnegie Institution of Washington. https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/35045009</ref> are 3–5.5 cm long and show a gradual transition towards the stamens.<ref name = "Flora of China" /> The petals decrease in size towards the centre of the flower.<ref name = "Flora of Pakistan" /> The androecium consists of 32–70 stamens.<ref name = "Conard, 1905" /> The gynoecium consists of 6–14 carpels.<ref name = "Henkel et al., 1907">Henkel, F., Rehnelt, F., Dittmann, L. (1907). [https://archive.org/details/Henkel_Nymphaeaceen/page/n84/mode/1up Das Buch der Nymphaeaceen oder Seerosengewächse.] pp. 83–84. Deutschland: Henkel.</ref> The red or yellow stigmatic disk<ref name = "Flora of Pakistan" /> is concave.<ref name = "Flora of Pakistan" /><ref name = "Gartenteich Ratgeber, 2022" /><ref name = "Pflanzen in Deutschland" /> The green to red, ovoid to spherical, 1.9–4.4 cm wide fruit with persistent sepals bears ellipsoid, brown, arillate,<ref name = "Conard, 1905" /> 4-6 mm long,<ref name = "FinBIF" /> and 3-4 mm wide seeds.<ref name = "Flora of Pakistan" />

===Cytology===
The chromosome count is 2n = 112, 160.<ref name = "Flora of China" /> The genome size is 1936.44 Mb.<ref name = "Chen et al., 2017">Chen, F., Liu, X., Yu, C., Chen, Y., Tang, H., & Zhang, L. (2017). [https://academic.oup.com/hr/article-pdf/doi/10.1038/hortres.2017.51/41958119/41438_2017_article_bfhortres201751.pdf "Water lilies as emerging models for Darwin’s abominable mystery."] Horticulture research, 4.</ref>

==Taxonomy==
The plant was described by [[Carl Borivoj Presl]] in 1882.<ref name = "Presl & Presl, 1822">Presl, Jan Svatopluk, & Presl, K. B. (1822). Deliciae pragenses, historiam naturalem spectantes (p. 224). Sumtibus Calve. https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/32211391</ref><ref name = "GBIF">{{Cite web|url=https://www.gbif.org/species/101391951|title=Nymphaea candida C. Presl - Checklist View|last=GBIF|website=www.gbif.org|access-date=2016-12-06}}</ref> However, sometimes both Carl Borivoj Presl and [[Jan Svatopluk Presl]] are credited as the taxon authors.<ref name = "Zhou et al., 2025" /><ref name = "FinBIF" /> Within the subgenus [[Nymphaea subg. Nymphaea|''Nymphaea'' subg. ''Nymphaea'']] it is placed in the section [[Nymphaea sect. Nymphaea|''Nymphaea'' sect. ''Nymphaea'']].<ref name = "GRIN">USDA, Agricultural Research Service, National Plant Germplasm System. 2025. Germplasm Resources Information Network (GRIN Taxonomy). National Germplasm Resources Laboratory, Beltsville, Maryland. URL: https://npgsweb.ars-grin.gov/gringlobal/taxon/taxonomydetail?id=415662. Accessed 19 March 2025.</ref>
===Etymology===
The specific epithet ''candida'' from the Latin ''candidus'' means pure white.<ref>Vecchia, M. (n.d.-a). ''Passiflora candida'' (Poepp. &Endl.) Mast. (1871). Passiflora. Retrieved March 19, 2025, from https://www.passiflora.it/candida/226/eng/</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
It grows in the quiet freshwaters in Eurasia. The plant grows only in water, as it is an aquatic plant, mainly in ponds, lakes, and slow flowing streams.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.naturalmedicinalherbs.net/herbs/n/nymphaea-candida.php|title=medicinal herbs: NYMPHAEA CANDIDA|website=www.naturalmedicinalherbs.net|access-date=2016-12-06}}</ref>

==Conservation==
It is endangered in China,<ref name = "Zhou et al., 2025">Zhou, X., Liu, H., Zhang, Y., & Guan, K. [https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/oryx/article/new-record-of-the-endangered-nymphaea-candida-discovered-in-xinjiang-china/648C39BAD79880C47E6B2166FF3EEF7D New record of the Endangered Nymphaea candida discovered in Xinjiang, China.] Oryx, 1-1.</ref> and Germany.<ref>Rettung für die Glänzende Seerose. (2024, July 29). Baden-Württemberg Regierungspräsidien. Retrieved March 19, 2025, from https://rp.baden-wuerttemberg.de/rps/seiten/aktuellemeldung/rettung-fuer-die-glaenzende-seerose/</ref>

==Use==
It is cultivated as an ornamental plant in water gardens.<ref name = "Gartenteich Ratgeber, 2022">Glänzende Seerose ''Nymphaea candida''. (2022, April 13). Gartenteich Ratgeber. Retrieved March 19, 2025, from https://www.gartenteich-ratgeber.com/pflanzen/wasserpflanzen/seerosen/glaenzende-seerose/</ref><ref name = "Hensel et al., 2011">Hensel, W., Hudak, R., Leute, A., Mayer, J. (2011). [https://www.google.de/books/edition/Garten_Das_Gr%C3%BCne_von_GU/RQijmMKs6_IC?hl=de&gbpv=1&dq=%22Nymphaea%20candida%22&pg=PA386&printsec=frontcover Garten - Das Grüne von GU: Gartenpraxis Schritt für Schritt.] p. 386. Deutschland: GRÄFE UND UNZER Verlag GmbH.</ref>
